subject: [Urgent] WebSocket stream p99 surge during peak - customer impact (NebulaAI)
messages:
From: Chris Alvarez <chris.alvarez@nebulaai.com>
To: support@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Streaming chat websocket p99 spikes during 5pm-6pm PST (today)

Hi Redwood team,

We're seeing a sharp regression in p99 latency on the streaming chat websocket endpoint during our evening peak (approx 17:00-18:00 PST). Between 17:05 and 17:30 our clients reported frequent stalls and reconnects. From our side:
- p95 increased from ~220ms to ~1.1s; p99 has been spiking to 8-12s (many streaming frames delayed).
- Error rate: increased websocket disconnects and application-level stream resets; upstream 502/504s visible.
- Traffic spike: ~2.2x normal concurrent connections for that window.

We captured several request IDs and a short trace archive (attached) that shows long queuing on proxy > worker handoff and unusually high connection churn. This is customer-facing and causing user complaints. Please escalate.

Requesting: immediate investigation, temporary mitigation to stop reconnect storm (route to dedicated pool or enable fallback), and ETA for root cause. We need a follow-up within 30 mins if possible.

Attached: nebula_traces_may03.zip (5MB stub)

Thanks,
Chris Alvarez
Head of Platform
NebulaAI

On Mon, May 3, 2027 at 4:20 PM Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks for the report, Chris — sorry you're seeing this. I'm escalating to SRE and CS. Dylan / Marissa, can you triage immediately and confirm a mitigation plan?

Initial triage notes (15m):
- We see a correlated spike across our edge proxies in us-west-2 coincident with Nebula traffic. Connection churn up ~2x, queue length on worker processes up ~6-8x.
- Autoscaler logs show several new worker pools launched but with slow warm-up; autoscaling/placement latencies caused a backlog at the proxy level.
- There is a recent change in the release from last night that adjusted the batching window and the per-worker max connections (INF-8679). The timing aligns.

Immediate mitigations I'm proposing now:
1) Route Nebula traffic to the Dedicated fallback pool for the next 90 minutes (will require approval from product/ops).
2) Temporarily lower keepalive timeout and reduce per-worker max concurrent streams to limit head-of-line blocking.
3) Roll back the batching-window tweak on the affected pool or increase worker warm-up weight.

I've attached initial traces and a short playbook for this class of incidents. If we do a routing change, we should also provision burst capacity to avoid throttling.

Attachments: initial_traces.zip (logs + spans, stub), mitigation_playbook.pdf

I'll start the routing check now — will update in 10 mins with an ETA for the routing action.

-Dylan
Senior SRE
Redwood Inference

Team — updating with status and requesting exec approval for temporary capacity and credit authority. Summary:
- Impact: NebulaAI experienced sustained p99 spikes (8-12s) and session reconnects during their 17:05-17:30 PST window. SRE traced the problem to autoscaler/warm-up delays after last night's release (INF-8679) and head-of-line effects from increased per-worker concurrency.
- Mitigation taken: Dylan routed Nebula traffic to Dedicated fallback pool and reduced per-worker concurrency/keepalive; initial metrics show p99 dropping toward baseline (~1.6s at last check) and errors reduced.
- Request: Approval to (1) request a temporary Dedicated burst (1.5x capacity) for the next 6 hours to stabilize; (2) approve a one-time customer credit up to $4,000 if impact persists through tomorrow's peak.

Dylan — confirm cost/ops acceptance. Vivek / Sean — please advise; I need a go/no-go on the burst and credit to communicate to the customer.
